title: In the street
description: Name the things in a street, and say where you walk.
grammar: gender and articles, and prepositions of place
grammarNote: The street is a set of nouns, and estar tells you where each one is.

explanation.summary: A street is a line of objects, and each one has a name and a gender. Once you can name them, you can describe where you are walking.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: La acera, la calzada, la farola, la parada, la glorieta and la escaparate are feminine. El bordillo, el semáforo, el cruce and el buzón are masculine. La calzada is the road itself, and la acera is the part you walk on.

sections.heading: Where things are
sections.body: Estar says where a thing is, and the place follows: el buzón está en la esquina, la parada está frente al banco. Frente and en el are the two you will use most in a street, and the noun after them keeps its article.

examples.es: el buzón está en la esquina
examples.en: the postbox is on the corner

examples.es: la parada está frente al banco
examples.en: the bus stop is opposite the bench

examples.es: la farola está al lado de la acera
examples.en: the street lamp is beside the pavement

items.note: Feminine: la acera. You walk on it, and cars drive on la calzada.
Masculine: el semáforo. The accent marks the stress.
Feminine: la parada. It is short for la parada de autobús.
Masculine: el buzón. The accent marks the stress.

drills.meaning: the roundabout is on the corner
the postbox has letters in it
